text: {"claims":[{"id":"c1","evidence":[{"sid":"P0.S0","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P1.S1","rel":"entails"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P0.S0 maps PostgreSQL Read Uncommitted to Read Committed; P1.S1 states Read Committed SELECTs exclude uncommitted concurrent data, so dirty reads are not exposed."},{"id":"c2","evidence":[{"sid":"P5.S2","rel":"entails"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P5.S2 explicitly says Serializable, like Repeatable Read, may require retries because of serialization failures."},{"id":"c3","evidence":[{"sid":"P4.S0","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P3.S2","rel":"entails"}],"check":{"kind":"version","left":"9.0","op":"<","right":"9.1"},"reasoning":"P4.S0 maps pre-9.1 Serializable to Repeatable Read behavior; P3.S2 says Repeatable Read still permits serialization anomalies."},{"id":"c5","evidence":[],"check":null,"reasoning":"P5.S4 mentions monitoring cost and no extra blocking, but does not establish that Serializable is actually slower than Repeatable Read."},{"id":"c6","evidence":[{"sid":"P6.S0","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P6.S1","rel":"entails"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P6.S0 identifies predicate locking; P6.S1 says those locks cause no blocking in PostgreSQL."},{"id":"c7","evidence":[{"sid":"P7.S0","rel":"refutes"},{"sid":"P7.S1","rel":"refutes"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P7.S0 says Serializable does not always prevent non-serial errors; P7.S1 gives unique constraint violations as an example, contradicting the absolute claim."},{"id":"c10","evidence":[],"check":null,"reasoning":"P5.S4 notes monitoring overhead but nothing supports a universal speed advantage for Repeatable Read over Serializable across every workload."}]}
